segments: 488. Chronography of Barhebraeus.
When these saw the multitude of the army of the Tatars, they despaired of fighting;
and at sunset they went out from the city to flee.
And when they reached the banks of the Jayhun (Oxus),
the road-guards of the Mongols fell upon them,
and destroyed them all with the edge of the sword.
Now when the citizens saw that they had no one to stand against them,
they opened the gates of the city,
and went to submit to Genghis Khan.
And he had mercy on them,
and did not kill them.
Rather, he entered the city to see it;
and when he reached the gate of the great mosque,
he asked,
"Is this the court of the ruler?" And the scribes of the Arabs said to him,
"No,
rather it is the house of God."
And Genghis Khan dismounted from his horse,
and entered and sat before the mihrab.
And Tolui, his younger son, ascended the steps of the minbar.
And Genghis Khan commanded:
"Our horses are hungry,
and the plain is devoid of grass."
So the notables of the city went and opened the granaries and pits of wheat and barley,
and carried them on their shoulders, brought them, and threw fodder to the horses,
and sat watching over them.
And they also brought wine-servers and gave drink to the Tatars,
as well as male and female singers,
and also other women who danced,
while in truth their hearts were trembling.
And Genghis Khan called the notables of the city and said to them thus:
"As for the treasures that are above the earth, we have no need for you to show them to us;
rather, those which are buried in the heart of the earth, we require you to bring out and give to us,
and you shall live."
And they said,
"May your command be fulfilled."
And they went and dug and brought out and presented wealth beyond reckoning.
And because the multitude of the warriors had hidden themselves in the city {OCR: ܒܵܗ̇ ܒܲܡܕܝܼܢ̄ܬܵܐ?},
they cast fire into it, and it all burned, along with everyone who was hidden in it.
And those who were outside were dispersed throughout the lands.
For when one man of Bukhara came to Khorasan, and they asked him,
"How did it happen with them?", he said,
"Why do you weary me? For the Tatars came, and they killed, and dug, and burned, and took captive, and went away.
He who has ears to hear, let him hear."
And in this same year, Bar Mashtub,
he who, as we said, had rebelled against al-Ashraf,
went toward Nisibis,
that from there he might cross over to Erbil to Muzaffar al-Din.
